## QUESTION|TASK 1

__Fix all of the varied missing data types in the data to be consistent (all missing values should be displayed as “NaN”).__ In your report include one record example (one row) from your new data, in the raw JSON format. Your example should display the "NaN" for at least one missing value.__  

I fixed all the varied missing data types in the dataset by standardizing them to `NaN` using pandas' `replace` method. This approach ensures that all representations of missing data, such as "NA", "NaN", "null", "None", and empty strings, are uniformly treated as `NaN`. This standardization is crucial for accurate data analysis and handling of missing values in subsequent computations. Below is an example of one record from the cleaned dataset in raw JSON format, which includes `NaN` for missing values.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here

df = df.replace(
    ["NA", "NaN", "null", "None", ""],
    np.nan
)

df.head()


```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
df.isna().sum()

```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here

example_row = df[df.isna().any(axis=1)].iloc[0]

example_row.to_json()


```


## QUESTION|TASK 2

__Which airport has the worst delays?__ Describe the metric you chose, and why you chose it to determine the “worst” airport. Your answer should include a summary table that lists (for each airport) the total number of flights, total number of delayed flights, proportion of delayed flights, and average delay time in hours.   

To identify the airport with the worst delays, the proportion of delayed flights was used as the primary metric, as it accounts for differences in airport size and reflects the likelihood that a passenger will experience a delay. Based on this measure, SFO (San Francisco International Airport) had the worst delays in the dataset. Out of 1,630,945 total flights, 425,604 flights were delayed, resulting in a delay proportion of approximately 26.1%. Additionally, the average delay duration for delayed flights at SFO was about 1.04 hours, indicating that delays at this airport are both frequent and substantial. While other airports may have higher total numbers of delayed flights, SFO stands out for consistently delaying a larger share of its flights.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here

airport_summary = (
    df.groupby("airport_code")
    .agg(
        total_flights=("num_of_flights_total", "sum"),
        total_delayed_flights=("num_of_delays_total", "sum"),
        total_delay_minutes=("minutes_delayed_total", "sum")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

airport_summary["proportion_delayed"] = (
    airport_summary["total_delayed_flights"] /
    airport_summary["total_flights"]
)

# Calculate 
airport_summary["avg_delay_hours"] = (
    airport_summary["total_delay_minutes"] /
    airport_summary["total_delayed_flights"]
) / 60

# Sort
airport_summary = airport_summary.sort_values(
    by="proportion_delayed",
    ascending=False
)

airport_summary.head()


```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
worst_airport = airport_summary.iloc[0]
worst_airport


```

## QUESTION|TASK 3

__What is the best month to fly if you want to avoid delays of any length?__ Describe the metric you chose and why you chose it to calculate your answer. Include one chart to help support your answer, with the x-axis ordered by month. (To answer this question, you will need to remove any rows that are missing the `Month` variable.)  

The results show that September is the best month to fly to avoid delays, with the lowest proportion of delayed flights at approximately 16.5%. This metric was chosen because it directly reflects the likelihood of experiencing a delay during a flight, making it a practical measure for travelers. The accompanying bar chart illustrates the proportion of delayed flights for each month, clearly showing that September has the lowest delay rate compared to other months.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
df_month = df.dropna(subset=["month"]).copy()

```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
month_summary = (
    df_month.groupby("month")
    .agg(
        total_flights=("num_of_flights_total", "sum"),
        total_delayed_flights=("num_of_delays_total", "sum")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

month_summary["proportion_delayed"] = (
    month_summary["total_delayed_flights"] /
    month_summary["total_flights"]
)

month_summary

```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
month_order = [
    "January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June",
    "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December"
]

month_summary["month"] = pd.Categorical(
    month_summary["month"],
    categories=month_order,
    ordered=True
)

month_summary = month_summary.sort_values("month")

```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
import altair as alt

alt.Chart(month_summary).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("month:N", title="Month", sort=month_order),
    y=alt.Y("proportion_delayed:Q", title="Proportion of Delayed Flights"),
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip("month:N", title="Month"),
        alt.Tooltip("proportion_delayed:Q", title="Proportion Delayed", format=".2%")
    ]
).properties(
    title="Proportion of Delayed Flights by Month",
    width=600,
    height=300
)

```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
best_month = month_summary.loc[
    month_summary["proportion_delayed"].idxmin()
]

best_month

```

## QUESTION|TASK 4

According to the BTS website, the “Weather” category only accounts for severe weather delays. Mild weather delays are not counted in the “Weather” category, but are actually included in both the “NAS” and “Late-Arriving Aircraft” categories. __Your job is to create a new column that calculates the total number of flights delayed by weather (both severe and mild).__ You will need to replace all the missing values in the Late Aircraft variable with the mean. Show your work by printing the first 5 rows of data in a table. Use these three rules for your calculations:  

    a. 100% of delayed flights in the Weather category are due to weather  
    a. 30% of all delayed flights in the Late-Arriving category are due to weather  
    a. From April to August, 40% of delayed flights in the NAS category are due to weather. The rest of the months, the proportion rises to 65%    

A new column was created to estimate total weather-related flight delays using BTS guidelines, incorporating both severe and mild weather effects. Severe weather delays were fully counted, while 30% of late-arriving aircraft delays and a seasonally adjusted proportion of NAS delays were attributed to weather. Based on the results, ORD experienced the highest estimated number of weather-related delays in January, followed by ATL, while SAN had the fewest. This demonstrates that accounting for mild weather provides a more accurate understanding of weather’s impact on flight delays than using severe weather delays alone.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here

late_aircraft_mean = df["num_of_delays_late_aircraft"].mean()

df["num_of_delays_late_aircraft"] = df["num_of_delays_late_aircraft"].fillna(late_aircraft_mean)

```


```{python}

low_weather_months = ["April", "May", "June", "July", "August"]

df["nas_weather_fraction"] = np.where(
    df["month"].isin(low_weather_months),
    0.40,
    0.65
)

```


```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
df["total_weather_delays"] = (
    df["num_of_delays_weather"] +
    0.30 * df["num_of_delays_late_aircraft"] +
    df["nas_weather_fraction"] * df["num_of_delays_nas"]
)

```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
df[
    [
        "airport_code",
        "month",
        "num_of_delays_weather",
        "num_of_delays_late_aircraft",
        "num_of_delays_nas",
        "total_weather_delays"
    ]
].head()

```



## QUESTION|TASK 5

__Using the new weather variable calculated above, create a barplot showing the proportion of all flights that are delayed by weather at each airport. Describe what you learn from this graph.__  
What I learned from this graph is that certain airports experience a higher proportion of weather-related delays compared to others. For instance, airports located in regions prone to severe weather conditions, such as SFO and IAD, tend to have a higher proportion of flights delayed due to weather. This information can be crucial for travelers when planning their trips, as it highlights the potential risks associated with flying from specific airports during certain times of the year. Additionally, airlines and airport authorities can use this data to improve their operational strategies and mitigate the impact of weather-related delays on passengers.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here

weather_summary = (
    df.groupby("airport_code")
    .agg(
        total_flights=("num_of_flights_total", "sum"),
        weather_delays=("total_weather_delays", "sum")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

weather_summary["prop_weather_delayed"] = (
    weather_summary["weather_delays"] /
    weather_summary["total_flights"]
)

weather_summary

```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
from lets_plot import *

ggplot(
    weather_summary,
    aes(x="airport_code", y="prop_weather_delayed")
) + \
geom_bar(stat="identity", fill="#4C72B0") + \
labs(
    title="Proportion of Flights Delayed by Weather",
    x="Airport",
    y="Proportion of Flights"
) + \
theme(axis_text_x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1))

```

## STRETCH QUESTION|TASK 1

__Which delay is the worst delay?__ Create a similar analysis as above for Weahter Delay with: Carrier Delay and Security Delay. Compare the proportion of delay for each of the three categories in a Chart and a Table. Describe your results.

The worst weather Delay was in San Fransisco (SFO) with a proportion of approximately 0.12. The worst Carrier Delay was in Atlanta (ATL) with a proportion of approximately 0.10. The worst Security Delay was in Washington Dulles (IAD) with a proportion of approximately 0.02. Overall, Weather Delays tend to have the highest proportions across most airports, followed by Carrier Delays, and then Security Delays, which are generally the least frequent. This indicates that weather conditions have a more significant impact on flight delays compared to carrier operations and security procedures.


```{python}
# Convert delay columns to numeric
cols_to_numeric = [
    "num_of_flights_total",
    "num_of_delays_carrier",
    "num_of_delays_security",
    "total_weather_delays"
]

for col in cols_to_numeric:
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

```


```{python}
# Include and execute your code here

delay_comparison = (
    df.groupby("airport_code")
    .agg(
        total_flights=("num_of_flights_total", "sum"),
        weather_delays=("total_weather_delays", "sum"),
        carrier_delays=("num_of_delays_carrier", "sum"),
        security_delays=("num_of_delays_security", "sum")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Calculate proportions
delay_comparison["prop_weather"] = delay_comparison["weather_delays"] / delay_comparison["total_flights"]
delay_comparison["prop_carrier"] = delay_comparison["carrier_delays"] / delay_comparison["total_flights"]
delay_comparison["prop_security"] = delay_comparison["security_delays"] / delay_comparison["total_flights"]

delay_comparison


```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here

delay_long = delay_comparison.melt(
    id_vars="airport_code",
    value_vars=["prop_weather", "prop_carrier", "prop_security"],
    var_name="delay_type",
    value_name="proportion"
)

delay_long["delay_type"] = delay_long["delay_type"].replace({
    "prop_weather": "Weather Delay",
    "prop_carrier": "Carrier Delay",
    "prop_security": "Security Delay"
})

delay_long


```

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
from lets_plot import *

ggplot(
    delay_long,
    aes(x="airport_code", y="proportion", fill="delay_type")
) + \
geom_bar(stat="identity", position="dodge") + \
labs(
    title="Proportion of Flights Delayed by Delay Type",
    x="Airport",
    y="Proportion of Flights",
    fill="Delay Type"
) + \
theme(axis_text_x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1))


```
